stem: Anemia is best defined as which change in red blood cells?

options.label: A
options.text: Red blood cells carrying carbon monoxide-bound hemoglobin
options.misconception: Mistakes blocked oxygen binding in normal red cells for too few red cells.
options.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin in normal numbers of red cells and blocks oxygen carriage; oxygen delivery falls, but red cell amount does not.

options.label: B
options.text: Red blood cells with high-oxygen-affinity hemoglobin
options.misconception: Equates poor oxygen unloading with too few healthy red cells.
options.explanation: High-affinity hemoglobin variants hold oxygen too tightly, and the resulting erythropoietin drive raises red cell numbers; this is erythrocytosis, not anemia.

options.label: C
options.text: Red blood cells with a raised methemoglobin fraction
options.misconception: Equates dysfunctional hemoglobin with a low red cell amount.
options.explanation: Methemoglobin carries oxidized heme iron that cannot bind oxygen; red cell numbers can be normal, so oxygen delivery falls but this is not anemia.

options.label: D
options.text: A lower-than-normal amount of healthy red blood cells
options.misconception: None — anemia is too few healthy red blood cells.
options.explanation: Anemia is a lower-than-normal amount of healthy red blood cells, so the body gets too little oxygen-rich blood; low production, destruction or blood loss can cause it.

options.label: E
options.text: A higher-than-normal hematocrit from plasma volume loss
options.misconception: Confuses a concentration change from lost plasma with a change in red cell production.
options.explanation: Plasma volume loss concentrates a normal red cell mass, a relative polycythemia; red cell amount is unchanged, so this is not anemia.

context: Learning objective: Anemia is a lower-than-normal amount of healthy red blood cells, so the body gets too little oxygen-rich blood.
